issues.description: DFS loop invariant is not stated after collapsing 'working' and 'walking' into one state
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the state machine went from three states to two without writing down the invariant that distinguishes a first visit (children just pushed) from a second visit (children drained). The push() cycle-detection branch and the iteration loop both depend on this distinction. A literate comment stating the invariant above the loop is required.

issues.description: Behavioral change on yield=false: state[k]=sorted now runs conditionally, changing the loop postcondition
issues.detail: Previously the node was marked sorted unconditionally after pop; now it only happens when yield returns true. The deferred clear() papers over this for reuse, but the postcondition has silently changed and is coupled across distant lines. State the new postcondition explicitly or a future maintainer will break it.

issues.description: Cleanup-on-defer substitutes for a stated Sort entry precondition and complects lifetime with identity
issues.detail: Moving clear(s.state) and clear(s.stack) into the defer is defensive-as-substitute for an explicit precondition ('on entry state is empty, stack length zero'). It also entangles iterator lifetime with sorter identity if yield panics or the caller abandons iteration. Establish the precondition; the defer is then merely how it is maintained.

issues.description: No regression test added for the Sort-twice-on-same-Sorter reuse bug the PR claims to fix
issues.detail: The PR title claims a state-reuse fix, but the diff contains no test calling Sort twice on the same Sorter and asserting the second result. A three-line regression test would lock in the reuse contract the defer now establishes. Testing shows presence of bugs, not absence — but the absence of any test is conspicuous.

issues.description: New comment contains typos ('visisted', 'if its') in the canonical state-machine explanation
issues.detail: The rewritten comment is the one place the two-visit DFS model is explained, and it now reads 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its' (should be 'it's'). Since the state machine just lost a state, this comment is doing more load-bearing work than before. Clean it up.

issues.description: clear(s.stack) + s.stack[:0] pair is correct but undocumented; intent (GC of Node references) is implicit
issues.detail: The old s.stack[0:] was a no-op that retained stale Node references. The new clear+truncate pair is exactly right but does two things at once with no comment explaining why clear precedes truncate. One line ('clear before reslice so retained Node references can be GC'd') would make the time-and-value story explicit.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch fixes two real defects — the no-op s.stack[0:] that retained Node references and state clobbering across Sort calls — and that collapsing 'working' into 'walking' is a reasonable simplification. But all three reviewers independently flag that the change is presented as a correctness fix without the discipline a correctness fix demands: no stated invariant for the two-visit DFS, no explicit entry precondition (the defer substitutes for one), and a silent change to the loop postcondition when yield returns false. Verdict: under-audited but likely correct. Require a literate comment stating the invariant and reuse precondition, a Sort-twice regression test, and a typo pass on the new comment before merging.
